resources.string: Preparation continues while you leave the app. You can cancel from the notification.
Image prepared and checked. Return to the app to select a USB target.
Preparation interrupted. Select the image and start again.
Android stopped preparation at its background time limit. Return to the app and start again.
Show the complete catalog without filtering by board.
Choose your Pi to filter the OS catalog. Compatibility follows the catalog information. Check local images yourself.
Changing the model clears the current image selection and first-boot settings. The cached file can be removed with Clear image and settings.
Search this category and its loaded subcategories. Open remote categories to search their contents.
No matching images. Clear the search, go back, or choose another model.
Write an operating system to a USB drive or SD card reader.
IMG, ISO, XZ, GZ or ZIP · prepared in private app storage
Connect a USB-OTG card reader. Eject its mounted volumes in Android first.
All data on %1$s (%2$s) will be overwritten with %3$s. Double-check the device. Never disconnect it during writing or verification.
The entire device is overwritten. A complete read-back check follows automatically.
Keep the USB device connected. You can leave this screen while writing.
Cancelled. A partly written device must be imaged again.
USB access was denied. Select the device to try again.
USB-OTG required · No root · Android 8+\nFirst-boot settings require a supported FAT32 boot image. Connect setup uses an auth key. Secure boot is not available.

Applied to the prepared image before writing. Account passwords are hashed; Wi-Fi credentials and Connect keys are written to the boot partition. Settings stay in this app session. Clear the image to remove its cached copy.
Choose the format supported by your local image. No automatic detection is performed.
Public-key authentication requires at least one public key. Never paste a private key.
Enable Raspberry Pi hardware interfaces at first boot.
This image contains a single-use Connect key. For another Pi, create a new key and prepare the image again.
Link the Pi to your Raspberry Pi Connect account at first boot. Create an auth key in your browser, then paste it here.
This catalog image does not advertise Connect support. Choose a compatible Raspberry Pi OS image.
For local images, Connect must already be installed with its sign-in service. The app does not install packages. Lite supports remote shell; screen sharing needs a Wayland desktop.
No browser available. Open https://connect.raspberrypi.com/settings on another device.

Use a new key for each Pi. Personal keys expire after 6 hours; organisation keys use their chosen expiry. Boot with internet access before expiry. The key is readable in the prepared image and on its boot partition until consumed. Clear the image and settings after use.
